doc.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024

title: Replacing Kenny Garrett on Miles's tour
summary: After one Stockholm gig Miles let Kenny go, called him back for a six-week tour with no rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: So I transcribed a couple of the melodies that I had heard already just so I was just ready to do that. But I didn’t really have to do that much playing of the melodies by myself because Kenny was there. And that was — this is also an amazing story. We were in Stockholm, that was the first gig. And after that gig Miles collapsed backstage. He fainted. So yeah, he was not in the best of health obviously. So the next day we were getting on the bus and he comes to me and says, “It’s too much energy to have another person on stage” because that means he has to figure out where to give somebody else an extra solo and kind of change — so he said, “I’ll call you when Kenny leaves.” So I played one gig and I flew back to New York like two days later. And I was like what just happened? Did I suck? Did he not like — you know all the questions. And I think it was about a month later they were getting ready to do their next leg of the tour which was six weeks. And he called me and said, “Kenny just left, we need you.” And the first gig I played was in Stockholm. So I started where I left off and from that point I did the six weeks without Kenny. And the show was the same and so no rehearsal, we just went out there and the band was exactly the same so I was just there but by myself, not with Kenny, and just playing little melodies and short little things that I needed to do and yeah, no rehearsals. And sound checks Miles was never there. We just went and checked the sound without him.
You can’t make this kind of thing up, can you?
